reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program
    Jurisdiction: Connecticut
    Focus year: 2021
    Question: Is the term 'Warrant for possession' used to refer to the order from the court
              to the authorities to remove a tenant?
*/

/* =========================
   Scenario (facts + helper)
   ========================= */

scenario_context(connecticut, 2021).

% The question asks about terminology: whether the term is used to refer to a court order to authorities.
scenario_term_under_question(warrant_for_possession).
scenario_meaning_under_question(order_from_court_to_authorities_to_remove_tenant).

% Helper predicate that succeeds when the encoded scenario statement holds.
scenario_statement :-
    scenario_context(connecticut, 2021),
    scenario_term_under_question(warrant_for_possession),
    scenario_meaning_under_question(order_from_court_to_authorities_to_remove_tenant).

/* ==========================================
   Statute translations (deterministic rules)
   ========================================== */

% --- CT Gen Stat  47a-35 (2020) ---
% (a) Execution stayed for five days from date judgment rendered (excluding Sundays/legal holidays).
statute_47a_35_stay_period_days(5).

% (b) No appeal except within such five-day period.
statute_47a_35_appeal_period_days(5).

% (b) If an appeal is taken within such period, execution is stayed until final determination,
% unless judge finds appeal solely for delay or defendant fails to give bond (47a-35a).
% We encode the core conditional logic at a high level (without modeling bond details).
statute_47a_35_execution_stayed_on_timely_appeal(yes).

% --- CT Gen Stat  47a-41a (2020) ---
% Execution to enforce a summary process judgment shall not be issued after six months from judgment,
% excluding any period during which execution was stayed.
statute_47a_41a_execution_limit_months(6).

/* ==========================================================
   Statutory vocabulary: which terms are used in these statutes
   ========================================================== */

% We model "term is used in the provided statute texts" as a closed set, so absence implies "not used".
% (The supplied statutes use "execution" and do not use "warrant for possession".)

statute_term_used(execution).

/* ======================================================
   Legal meaning mapping (conceptual meaning in eviction)
   ====================================================== */

% In Connecticut summary process practice, an "execution" enforces the judgment for possession and is
% the court's process directing an officer to carry out the removal/possession transfer.
% (This is a conceptual mapping for reasoning; it does NOT add the missing term to the statute text.)
term_means_in_summary_process(execution, order_from_court_to_authorities_to_remove_tenant).

/* ===================================================
   Reasoning helpers applying statute + scenario facts
   =================================================== */

% True when the relevant statutory materials use Term to refer to Meaning.
% This requires: (1) the term appears in the statute text set we encoded, AND
%               (2) the term is mapped to the meaning in the eviction context.
legal_term_used_to_refer_to(Term, Meaning) :-
    statute_term_used(Term),
    term_means_in_summary_process(Term, Meaning).

/* =====================
   Final answer predicate
   ===================== */

housing_answer(yes) :-
    scenario_statement,
    scenario_term_under_question(Term),
    scenario_meaning_under_question(Meaning),
    legal_term_used_to_refer_to(Term, Meaning),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    scenario_statement,
    !.

/* ==============
   Main entrypoint
   ============== */

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Is the term 'Warrant for possession' used to refer to the order from the court to the authorities to remove a tenant?
